standard_prerequisites.name: Truncation and its recursion principle
standard_prerequisites.statement: The truncation of a type to a level is k-truncated itself and maps into it are defined by the recursion principle, which requires the target to be k-truncated.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both maps of the equivalence are defined by that principle and their well-definedness rests on the truncation levels of their targets.

standard_prerequisites.name: n-type-ness is downward closed
standard_prerequisites.statement: A k-truncated type is also n-truncated whenever k is at most n.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reason the first map is well defined.

core_obligations: Define the map from the truncation at k of the truncation at n of A to the truncation at k of A by sending a k-projection of an n-projection of a to the k-projection of a, and check that it is well defined because the target is k-truncated and n-truncated with k at most n (source lines 748-759).
Define the map in the other direction by sending a k-projection of a to the k-projection of the n-projection of a, well defined because the target is k-truncated (source lines 748-759).
Show that the first composite is the identity on the truncation at k of A by evaluating it on a k-projection (source lines 761-762).
Show that the second composite is the identity on the truncation at k of the truncation at n of A in the same way, which closes the equivalence (source lines 762-763).

proof_roadmap.step: Write down the two maps by the truncation recursion principle.
Check well-definedness from the truncation levels of the targets.
Evaluate both composites on generators to get the two identities.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 743-746: for k at most n the iterated truncation collapses. The proof (source lines 747-764) is short but supplies the whole equivalence rather than a pointer: it defines the two maps by the recursion principle for truncations, verifies that each is well defined from the truncation level of its target (for the first one the level is exactly the hypothesis k at most n), and then checks both composites on the generating projections. The construction of the maps and the well-definedness checks are the substance and none of them is visible in the statement.
